# Iceland Winter 2025

## Overview

Five days in February 2025, the second week of the month, and I kept to the south coast the whole time. A small 4x4 on studded tyres, booked from a depot in Keflavik. I had driven the full Ring Road the previous summer and wanted to see the same places under snow without the long northern haul. Daylight ran about nine hours, which sounds generous until you subtract breakfast and half an hour of scraping ice. Temperatures sat between minus two and plus three, and the wind off the sea made it feel colder than the number.

## Route

I checked road.is every morning before leaving the guesthouse, and twice the route east of Vik carried a yellow warning. No F-roads were open in February, so the highland shortcuts were simply off the table and I did not miss them. Reykjavik to Selfoss on day one, then Skogafoss and the path behind the falls, then Vik for two nights. From Vik I went as far as the glacier lagoon at Jokulsarlon on the clearest day and turned back before dark. The last day retraced the coast west to Keflavik with a stop at the Blue Lagoon, crowded but warm.

## Costs

The 4x4 rental came to 620 euros for five days with the winter tyre package included, which I thought fair for the conditions. Fuel was 210 euros for roughly 900 km, diesel sitting near 3.10 euros a litre. Guesthouses ran 120 to 160 euros a night, and I ate most meals from a supermarket, maybe 18 euros a day. One dinner in Vik, lamb and potatoes, cost 55 euros with a beer. The lagoon entry was 70 euros. The whole trip landed close to 2100 euros.
